city_center.name: Minneapolis riverfront (Mill District / Stone Arch Bridge) + St. Paul
city_center.landmark: Stone Arch Bridge and the Mill District over the Mississippi; Minneapolis Farmers Market; the North Woods and lake country beyond the metro
city_center.notes: The Twin Cities sit on the Mississippi where the historic flour mills stood; the Stone Arch Bridge and Mill District anchor the riverfront. North of the metro lies Minnesota's North Woods and lake country -- wild rice, walleye, and pine. sources: en.wikipedia.org Stone Arch Bridge (Minneapolis); minneapolisfarmersmarket.com.

cultural_notes: the Twin Cities hold the largest Somali community in the US (Cedar-Riverside) and one of the largest Hmong communities (St. Paul) -- both major food-culture identities alongside a Nordic heritage (source: general demographic framing, publicly documented)

the Honeycrisp apple was bred at the University of Minnesota and is a point of state pride; Minnesota Grown is the state farm-produce program (source: University of Minnesota apple breeding; Minnesota Grown)

Minnesota's North Woods and lake country (the Land of 10,000 Lakes) frames cabin-and-lake culture; wild rice (manoomin) is a signature crop with deep cultural significance to Ojibwe communities -- reference respectfully, no tribal endorsement implied without consent (source: general framing; Ojibwe manoomin cultural note)
Cub Foods, Lunds & Byerlys, and Hy-Vee are the metro grocers (source: chain regional footprint)
